note:
The household of Alfred Bradley, cotton doubler, a single man keeping house with his niece, a visiting governess and three servants at 3 Park Terrace (#243) on the 1891 return, transcribed by A. Hagues. None of the six was in the record, and 3 Park Terrace held only 1921, so 1891 is free and nothing is displaced.

**A Bradley holds number 3 for thirty years.** Wright's Directory prints 'Mr. Charles Bradley' at 3 Park Terrace in 1894-95 and 1898-99, then 'Bradley Herbert' in 1910-11, 1913-14 and 1915-16; the record already has Herbert Bradley (#1796, born 1848) there on the 1921 return. With Alfred here in 1891, three Bradleys of the same generation follow one another at the house. They are very likely brothers, but the censuses and directories say nothing about how they are related, so no family links are made and Alfred is not bound to Herbert - the forenames and birth years differ (Alfred born 1846, Herbert 1848).

Eleanor Jane Gill is the head's niece, so her mother was probably a Bradley sister; she is not the Alice Margaret Gill already in the record (#1817, born 1873, at 13 Park Terrace in 1921), and no link is made because the return does not name her parents. Two servant surnames look like index renderings rather than settled spellings and are entered as transcribed: Martha Troobey and Sarah J Mauney. Ages are as the enumerator wrote them, so a birth year worked back from one may be a year out either way.
source: 1891 census, 3 Park Terrace, transcribed by A. Hagues. Directory evidence: Wright's Directory of Nottingham 1894-95, page 107 (Leicester Special Collections id 164613); 1898-99, page 115 (id 165291); 1910-11, page 154 (id 165830); 1913-14, page 172 (id 166528); 1915-16, page 174 (id 347815).
